items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] AI in health care offers many cases that regulatory frameworks should be addressing. A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: AI Has Entered the Boardroom. Who’s Overseeing It? | Stanford Graduate School of Business
items.summary:
In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. Matthys says that board members would ideally like to use AI “to track and summarize board packages and more quickly understand year-to-year trends by using LLM tools rather than reading 80- to 100-page reports.” [...] The sooner the better, the researchers suggest. “Moving too slowly with AI governance means you may miss out on opportunities,” Saripalli says. “The board has fiduciary responsibility for anything that has impact at the product or service level.”

“The risk of not moving is as serious as the risk of AI systems running amok,” Matthys adds, noting how past technological shifts have left unprepared companies behind. “If you don’t keep up, there’s a risk that 20 years from now you won’t exist.” [...] ## In Brief

 A new survey finds that corporate boards are not keeping up with AI governance.
 Directors report that they are discussing and using AI, yet their boards lack a systematic approach to oversight.
 Companies that wait to define AI strategy and audit their AI use risk being left behind.

“We’re trying to change the wheels on the bus while driving it at 100 miles an hour downhill.”

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.  

Wang also developed an AI elective within the School of Pharmacy, focused on practical applications for future clinicians. [...] “Every pharmacist has heard the rumors that AI will take pharmacists’ jobs,” Wang said. “But early exposure helps students. As future clinicians, they learn where the real focus should be in relation to AI. That’s something my students learn in this course.”  

Wang also works with students on research projects, extending that learning beyond the classroom. Two PharmD students, Elena Wu ’27 and Harvey Duong ’27, have collaborated with her on studies using AI to analyze large datasets.

items.title: Việt Nam - Nhật Bản hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào trị ung thư
items.summary:
Công nghệ tế bào gốc trung mô (MSC) hiện được nghiên cứu, phát triển trong nhiều hướng ứng dụng liên quan đến bệnh lý tim mạch, thần kinh (đột quỵ, sa sút trí tuệ), tiểu đường, bệnh phổi tắc nghẽn mạn tính (COPD), trẻ hóa da… Giải pháp tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên (NK) mở ra cơ hội ứng dụng mới trong miễn dịch trị liệu, có thể được phối hợp với các phương pháp điều trị ung thư đa mô thức khác, như phẫu thuật, hóa trị, xạ trị và điều trị đích. [...] Hai bên lựa chọn chuyển giao các công nghệ tế bào thế hệ mới, được Tập đoàn Y tế Grandsoul, Nhật Bản nghiên cứu, phát triển và ứng dụng. Bộ Y tế, Lao động và Phúc lợi Nhật Bản (MHLW) đã phê duyệt, cấp phép ứng dụng chính thức nhiều năm tại nước này. Trọng tm gồm hai nhóm: công nghệ phn lập, nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào gốc trung mô có nguồn gốc từ mô mỡ (Mesenchymal Stem Cells - MSC) và công nghệ phn lập nuôi cấy, biệt hóa chọn lọc tế bào miễn dịch tự nhiên NK (Natural Killer cells) điều [...] ### Từ tiếp nhận công nghệ đến năng lực tự chủ tại Việt Nam

Ông Ngô Chí Dũng, Chủ tịch HĐQT Hệ thống Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tm Anh, cho biết việc hoàn tất chuyển giao công nghệ tế bào gốc và tế bào miễn dịch từ Nhật Bản là dấu mốc quan trọng không chỉ trong hợp tác y tế hai nước, mà còn là kết nối công nghệ, thiết lập mạng lưới chuyên gia vì mục tiêu chung là chăm sóc sức khỏe cho người dn.

items.title: Andrej Karpathy:
items.summary:
Andrej Karpathy:

“A 1B model can be much more effective than most current LLMs.

90% of current models waste a ton of capacity and money on remembering stuff that doesn’t matter.”

here is his 5 core thesis about Small LLM’s:

1. the intelligence was never the knowledge. Strip the memorized internet, keep the reasoning. What’s left is the cognitive core, and it’s small.

2. the core might fit in ~1B params. Maybe less. “Plenty of room at the bottom.” We’ve been paying for a library when we needed a brain.

3. size stopped being the bottleneck. What makes an agent work is the tools it can call and how tight the feedback loop is, not parameter count.

4. intelligence lives in the system, not the weights. A raw LLM is a CPU with no OS. Small core + good harness > giant model alone.

5. you can own it. A model on your hardware is one no one can rate-limit, price-hike, or deprecate on you.

in 12 months the gap between teams shipping on-device and teams paying per-token frontier bills won’t be capability.

TwIL an 8.8B model at 90%+ of frontier isn’t a benchmark flex.

It’s the thesis Karpathy’s been repeating all year, made real.

items.title: The AI Race is Putting Patients at Risk - Progressive.org
items.summary: Indeed, the most frightening risks involving AI are already moving from theory to capability. Frontier models let non-experts code new applications quickly, and soon it may be possible to use AI to create biological agents that can be weaponized. The White House’s own AI Action Plan warns that AI could create new pathways for bad actors to synthesize dangerous pathogens and calls for stronger screening and national security assessment of AI tools and systems. Anthropic has already said its [...] AI in health care offers many cases that regulatory frameworks should be addressing. A hospital can use AI for patient care and clinical decision support; an insurer for utilization management (e.g., automating care denials); a teenager for mental health advice; a public health department for outbreak detection; and a bad actor for infiltrating a hospital network. Different uses carry different risks and require separate risk-benefit analysis for determining regulatory guardrails. [...] Japan created an AI Strategy Headquarters headed by the prime minister and adopted a national AI basic plan. The United Kingdom and Australia are linking their AI safety institutes in order to better evaluate frontier AI model risks. These systems differ, but they have one thing in common - national AI governance.

items.title: AI Has Entered the Boardroom. Who’s Overseeing It? | Stanford Graduate School of Business
items.summary:
In the survey, 75% of directors said they used AI for research and market analysis, 55% for board prep and material summarization. Other common uses included strategic question generation and competitive benchmarking. Matthys says that board members would ideally like to use AI “to track and summarize board packages and more quickly understand year-to-year trends by using LLM tools rather than reading 80- to 100-page reports.” [...] The sooner the better, the researchers suggest. “Moving too slowly with AI governance means you may miss out on opportunities,” Saripalli says. “The board has fiduciary responsibility for anything that has impact at the product or service level.”

“The risk of not moving is as serious as the risk of AI systems running amok,” Matthys adds, noting how past technological shifts have left unprepared companies behind. “If you don’t keep up, there’s a risk that 20 years from now you won’t exist.” [...] ## In Brief

 A new survey finds that corporate boards are not keeping up with AI governance.
 Directors report that they are discussing and using AI, yet their boards lack a systematic approach to oversight.
 Companies that wait to define AI strategy and audit their AI use risk being left behind.

“We’re trying to change the wheels on the bus while driving it at 100 miles an hour downhill.”

items.title: Chapman Advances Healthcare AI Research and Training | Chapman Newsroom
items.summary:
Totonchy sees the skepticism around AI in higher education as an opportunity.  

“Generative AI quickly gained a negative reputation because it was seen as a tool for cheating,” she said. “That misses the point. These tools can work alongside humans, handling routine tasks so people can focus on analysis and decision-making. The sooner institutions move past resistance, the sooner AI can support that work.” 

STUDENTS PUT AI TO WORK [...] To address bias in clinical decision-making tools, Wang founded the Healthcare AI Initiative (HAI) at Chapman, bringing together researchers working on pressing healthcare challenges. HAI examines ethical questions surrounding AI, including data privacy, and develops equitable machine learning approaches.  

Wang also developed an AI elective within the School of Pharmacy, focused on practical applications for future clinicians. [...] “Every pharmacist has heard the rumors that AI will take pharmacists’ jobs,” Wang said. “But early exposure helps students. As future clinicians, they learn where the real focus should be in relation to AI. That’s something my students learn in this course.”  

Wang also works with students on research projects, extending that learning beyond the classroom. Two PharmD students, Elena Wu ’27 and Harvey Duong ’27, have collaborated with her on studies using AI to analyze large datasets.

items.title: Aguascalientes students take top robotics prizes
items.summary:
The Aguascalientes team, nicknamed Lanceros Overclock, won the high school division (ages 14 to 20) of Robo Shuttle at ROBOchæmpions, held Saturday and Sunday in the city of Lörrach. 

The competition required the budding scientists to work in teams of two or four to build and program autonomous robots that would perform predetermined tasks. (Phaenovum) [...] Overall, 16 students from Aguascalientes competed, but the names of the winners were not included in official results.

According to organizer Phaenovum — a student research center in Lörrach, Germany — the inaugural competition hosted teams from Mexico and Egypt in addition to regional competitors. It succeeded RoboRAVE Germany, a previous local version of RoboRAVE.

The organizer published results in five categories spanning races, robot duels, transport tasks and autonomous firefighting. [...] One challenge required robots to extinguish a candle flame autonomously.

Teams prepared and tested their robots Saturday before Sunday’s judging, awards ceremony and public demonstrations.

items.title: Twin brothers build 'Blast Robotics' team for kids in Philly region - 6abc Philadelphia
items.summary:
-- The Ponugoti twins put their brains together to help kids to blast off into the world of robotics.

Vivaan & Virat Ponugoti are juniors at Conestoga High School and live in Wayne, Pennsylvania. The pair always enjoyed science and technology, but didn't get interested in robotics until high school.

However, one brother did not make the team during their freshman year.

This was the spark that fueled their mission to provide more access to robotics opportunities for kids in the region. [...] They got their program off the ground through fundraising, social media outreach and word of mouth.

Blast Robotics, also known as Team 10989, launched last year and already has roughly 40 members on board.

Blast Robotics is a FMA (FIRST Mid Atlantic) team, part of Mid Atlantic Robotics. They recently competed in the 'Ramp Riot,' the 26th Annual Robotics Competition at Wissahickon High School. [...] The program is fueled by many community partners such as Eadeh Enterprises, who donated workshop space to the group.

"From summer camps, to raising monies to support the robotics mission and being an inclusive environment where everyone is learning, leading and thinking about the common goal is incredible," said Stacey H. Ballard, President & CEO of Eadeh Enterprises and member of the board.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] The artificial intelligence company said in its commitments that for data centers it owns and operates, it will solicit community input, publish construction plans and stay away from use of non-disclosure agreements with public officials. Additionally, in a policy blueprint, OpenAI encouraged policymakers to enact similar commitments as laws. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

items.title: Exclusive: OpenAI targets Microsoft's GitHub with deal
items.summary:
OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer, a developer tools startup whose technology is already embedded in Codex, the company told Axios exclusively.

Why it matters:OpenAI is joining a slew of companies challenging Microsoft's GitHub as AI agents take on more coding work. The platform has acted as a central repository and nerve center for software development for many years.

Zoom out:GitHub has faced a number of reliability issues and outages as AI coding has taken off. [...] Financial terms were not disclosed. Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source.

Between the lines:Earlier this week, OpenAI revealed Pando, built to handle the explosion of code generated by AI agents.

   OpenAI says Pando reduced the time needed to push code changes by nearly 80%. 
   The company is now exploring ways to make the technology available to customers. [...] Cursor, now owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, launched GitHub rival Origin in August.
   Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, who launched a new coding startup, announced a competing product last month.
   Microsoft owns nearly a quarter of OpenAI, although the two companies also compete in a variety of ways, a dynamic that is common across the competitive AI landscape.

Driving the news: OpenAI plans to integrate Pierre's Code Storage function into Codex, where Pierre's technology is already used.
